title: observability: token-level KV cost & latency dashboard + alert tuning for cache hotspots
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: production incidents in Jan-Feb showed KV-cache hotspots driving token-level cost and tail latency for long-context workloads. This PR adds a token-level KV cache dashboard, enriches existing token cost/latency breakdowns with KV-specific dimensions, and tunes several alerts to reduce noisy paging while preserving SLO coverage. Summary of changes: - New Grafana dashboard: 'KV Token Cost & Latency' (panels for per-route KV hit/miss rate, per-token cost contribution, 95/99/99.9 latencies partitioned by KV hit/miss). - Metric additions: redwood.kv.token_cost_total, redwood.kv.token_latency_seconds_bucket, redwood.kv.cache_hit_ratio (labels: env, region, model, route, customer_tier). - Logging: added structured KV-context fields to the inference span (kv.keys_cached_count, kv.variant, kv.eviction_reason) and ensured those fields are scrubbed for PII. - Tracing: span attributes for KV lookups added to serving runtime: kv_lookup.duration_ms and kv_lookup.result. - Alert tuning: adjusted thresholds and grouping to reduce pager noise for transient spikes, added a burn-rate style alert for sustained elevated per-token cost on KV misses over 30m, and an auto-snooze policy for non-prod clusters. - Backwards-compatible: metrics and dashboards are additive; all old metrics continue to work. Checklist: - [x] Metric names reviewed with metrics steward (ENG-3421) - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON exported and schema-validated - [x] Unit tests for metric tagging and PII scrubbing added - [x] Load test run against perf-canary replicating KV hotspot scenario - [x] Change log/release notes entry included Implementation notes: commits are small and scoped: runtime instrumentation in serving/kv_instrumentation.go, metrics registration in telemetry/metrics.go, dashboard JSON under observability/dashboards/kv-token-cost.json, alert rules in observability/alerts/kv_cost_rules.yaml, and minor docs in docs/observability/kv-token-cost.md. CI: initial CI run failed on linter for a column width in the dashboard JSON export; fixed and re-ran, final CI is green. Rollout plan: - Canary rollout to perf-canary cluster for 24h - Monitor new burn-rate alert and token-cost dashboard for false positives - Gradual rollout to prod regions with 1-hour pause between regions if alerts trip. Backout: remove new alert rules and toggle off instrumentation flag (runtime flag added) if we observe regressions. Related: SUP-881 (support case showing high token cost on customer X), INT-412 (internal postmortem follow-up). Links: Linear references: https://linear.app/org/issue/ENG-3421, Dashboard preview: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/kv-token-cost, Alert rules: observability/alerts/kv_cost_rules.yaml

release_notes: Added KV token-level cost/latency dashboard and tuned alerts to reduce noisy pagers. New metrics: redwood.kv.token_cost_total, redwood.kv.token_latency_seconds_bucket, redwood.kv.cache_hit_ratio. Rollout will be canary-first and monitored for 24h.
notes: This change helps SREs and runtime engineers quickly identify KV-cache miss patterns that drive token-level cost and tail latency. We expect reduced mean time to detection (MTTD) for KV-related regressions.
regression_risks: low - metrics and dashboards are additive. Risk comes from potential increased logging volume; mitigated by PII scrubbing and sampling defaults.
testing_performed: Unit tests added (telemetry/kv_metrics_test.go), integration perf-canary run replicating KV-hotspot workload, manual inspection of dashboard panels and alert behavior in staging.
post_merge_actions: Monitor new burn-rate alert for 48h, escalate to ENG-3421 if sustained cost increase or noisy alerts are observed; collect dashboard snapshots at +6h, +24h.
